title: My speech code
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Dealings with others and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y9 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF worksheet: my speech code)
intro: Lesson 33: Good speech: speak good or be silent. To understand the Islamic standard for speech and how it applies to lying, tale-carrying and online comments

questions.q: Explain the Islamic teaching on speech. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Speak good or be silent (Bukhari and Muslim); a good word is like a good tree (14:24); tale-carrying is a major sin (Bukhari and Muslim).
questions.model: Point 1: the rule. Develop: 'let him speak good or remain silent' (Bukhari and Muslim). Point 2: the value of a good word. Develop: like a good tree with firm roots (14:24).

questions.q: Write your personal 'speech code' in the portal response box: five rules for speaking and posting, each with evidence from this lesson or the last. Start: 'Rule 1: ...'
questions.a: Five clear rules with evidence (speak good or be silent; no gheebah 49:12; no namimah; truthfulness; three filters)
questions.model: Teacher writes rule 1: 'Before I post, I ask: is it true, is it needed, is it kind? (Speak good or be silent: Bukhari and Muslim.)'

questions.q: why is a joke that includes a lie still a problem?
questions.a: Lying is not allowed even in jest; the Prophet ﷺ joked but only spoke truth

questions.a: When we cannot say something good
